title: Learn tone pairs, not single tones
summary: Drill the tone contours in two-syllable pairs so your mouth learns movement, not labels.
attribution: Original content authored for this project.

blocks.body: A tone you can name is not a tone you can say. Instead of practising one syllable at a time, drill pairs that cover the transitions: high plus rising, falling plus neutral, third plus third. Two syllables force your voice to move, which is the actual skill. Keep one word fixed and change the word in front of it, for example 老师 lǎoshī (teacher) after a surname, as in 王老师 Wáng lǎoshī and 李老师 Lǐ lǎoshī. Read each pair slowly four times a day. If a pair feels flat and identical, your first tone is too low; keep it high and level before you chase the other shapes.

blocks.title: Try these pairs
body: 天空 tiānkōng — open sky (first plus first)
学习 xuéxí — to study (second plus second)
礼貌 lǐmào — polite (third plus fourth)
再见 zàijiàn — goodbye (fourth plus fourth)
妈妈 māma — mother (first plus neutral)
